ILLUSTRATIVE DELIVERABLE

Useful findings.
Clear next steps.

A fictional example for “Example Business Ltd”. No real practice or system was assessed. This demonstrates report structure, not scan results.

Example only · 14 November 2026

All facts, findings, owners and timeframes below are invented for demonstration. There is no security score, certification or assurance of safety.

1. Scope and method

Illustrative scope: business email, booking-account administration and recovery responsibilities. Hypothetical methods: owner discussion and owner-led settings review. Actual systems reviewed: none.

Excluded: client records, supplier infrastructure, device forensics, intrusive testing and compliance assessment. An actual engagement would name the authorised accounts, evidence dates and reviewer.

2. Executive explanation

In this fictional scenario, recovery ownership needs documenting and shared access needs clarification. Unknown controls are questions to resolve, not proven failures or evidence of compromise.

EXAMPLE A · TO VERIFY

Account recovery has no documented owner

Evidence status: hypothetical customer report only. No account settings inspected.

Business implication: unclear responsibility could delay restoring appointments after an account lockout.

Action: identify the recovery owner and confirm the procedure without placing recovery secrets in the report.

Suggested owner: business owner with IT support. Effort: small. Suggested timeframe: next working week, subject to verification.

EXAMPLE B · NOT ASSESSED

Two-factor authentication coverage is unknown

Evidence status: no observation or test. Unknown is not equivalent to disabled.

Business implication: the business cannot yet demonstrate which accounts have additional sign-in protection.

Action: arrange an owner-led settings check and record coverage and exceptions. Do not collect passwords or authentication codes.

Suggested owner: account administrator. Effort: depends on account count. Suggested timeframe: agreed during scoping.

3. Evidence labels

Not assessed
No review of this control was performed.
Customer-reported
A person described it; independent confirmation is outstanding.
Observed
A specific record or setting was seen at a recorded time.
Confirmed within scope
Evidence supports a limited conclusion for the agreed check, not for the whole business.

4. Handover and review

An actual report should assign each action, explain completion evidence and record remaining unknowns. Review dates follow the agreed scope; the fictional next-review date here is 14 December 2026. Neither a completed action nor an absence of findings guarantees that an incident cannot occur.
